content: User-facing fabro validate messages must be built as single-line format! strings (multi-line only via backslash-newline continuations verified by compilation), and the rule test must assert the EXACT expected message text, not substring containment. Substring assertions let mangled literals (embedded whitespace runs from scripted edits) pass review and ship garbled CLI output.

description: Cross-language string editing silently mangles Rust line continuations
resolution: Fixed in the fabro-900e review round: rewrote the two diagnostics in context_append_keys_within_allow.rs with real backslash-newline continuations and exact-equality assertions in the rule test (commit dc5959a80).

title: Per-node tool policy: allow-only explicit lists — no presets, no deny, no run-level list
rationale: Decided 2026-08-27 grilling for fabro-47b5 (ADR-0009 amendment). One attribute tools=<canonical names>, unset = default open. Presets are a blackbox in the graph and leak-free explicit lists self-document; deny lists cannot express read-only safely (MCP tools are run-config-dependent, future native tools leak); a run-level allowlist reintroduces replace-vs-narrow two-layer ambiguity. Presets may return later if lists grow unwieldy.

name: PermissionLevel origin: upstream interactive CLI approval axis
description: PermissionLevel (ReadOnly/ReadWrite/Full) was introduced upstream 2026-02-23 (Bryan Helmkamp, agent CLI approval callback). Enforced ONLY in the interactive CLI path via is_auto_approved(level, tool_category) at fabro-agent cli.rs ~153 (--permissions flag, default ReadWrite). Wire-contracted in OpenAPI (run events + projection). Workflow sessions report Full truthfully (no approval gating) and must never derive or remove it; tool restriction is a separate axis projected via agent_tools.

name: Upstream ownership map: tool-policy surfaces
description: Verified 2026-08-28 vs upstream/main (merge-base 56e759d47, 2026-08-26): ToolAccessPolicy/ToolAccess/ToolExposureMode + SessionOptions.tool_access_policy are upstream-owned and byte-identical in config.rs; the 'Override per-stage' comment in fabro-workflow api.rs ~1086-1089 is upstream's own words (per-stage tool attribute is their invited direction); NamedToolAccessPolicy exists upstream only as a test struct in session.rs tests; AskFabroToolAccessPolicy is upstream production pattern (canonical_tool_name matching); fabro-tool crate is upstream-owned (our only local addition: fabro_run_logs); PermissionLevel enforced only in interactive CLI (is_auto_approved, cli.rs ~153). graph.rs is our most-diverged file (204 lines from 900e+preamble work). Offer order when upstream reacts: 900e then 47b5.

name: upstream-v0.339-daytona-images-sql-line
description: Upstream v0.339.0-nightly.1 (merged 4a22e3d47, 2026-08-31): Daytona environments now accept image.docker (snapshot base image, DaytonaSnapshotSource enum in fabro-sandbox config). Fork consequence: our validate_daytona_image_settings rejection was removed as superseded; mutual-exclusion for docker provider (fabro-969f) kept in validate_docker_image_settings; from_environment.rs maps both providers through shared sandbox_dockerfile_source(). New SQL line: fabro-db migrations 2026082601_automation_run_targets, 2026082701_run_events, 2026082801_automation_environments + inactive SQL run-record store (RunSummaryStore name kept until cutover) — future state-to-SQL work must build on this line.

name: inspects-scope-defense-in-depth
description: ADR-0011 inspection scope (fabro-0c32, 5dd9ad8ca): graph attribute inspects=slug-list is the single authority declaration; it flows graph -> worker-token claim (coupled to agent:run_tools, issuance in worker_launch_spec) -> FabroRunToolServices.inspects (runner decodes own claims) -> tool registration gate + client-side target checks -> server-side per-route re-checks (RequiredAskFabroActor + target run workflow_slug; list_runs mandatory filter). Five layers, one declaration. Pattern for any future cross-workflow authority: name the capability in the graph, never the motive (inspects not revises — user decision, ADR-0011 amendment).

name: per-node-tool-policy
description: fabro-47b5 (c867a1a8): node attribute tools='read_file,grep' builds a NamedToolAccessPolicy (allow-only canonical names, profile vocab canonicalized both sides, question tools exempt both ways) threaded into SessionOptions + child SessionFactory; fabro_tools='fabro_run_get' is the inverse (default-denied opt-in overriding run.agent.fabro_tools). permission_level stays Full (wire-contracted CLI approval axis). Validation catalogs live as static lists in fabro-validate with dev-dep cross-check tests against the live crates — no production dependency edge.

title: Ask-Fabro terminal runs own sandbox liveness per turn
rationale: Session-held liveness without eviction machinery was impossible (SessionRuntimeEntry never removes entries); the projected runtime_context rebuilds conversations statelessly, so turn scope gives the no-leak guarantee of the inspection guard without a refcounted session-lifecycle system. User-facing leak (browsing finished runs, revisor fabro_ask targets) fixed with the smallest lifecycle concept that closes it.

name: interview-route-notifications
description: fabro-36d2 (789d76734): interview questions are now notifiable lifecycle events. Route key = the real event name 'interview.started' (route events lists are plain strings matched against event_name(); introducing a 'question.pending' alias would add vocabulary + a mapping layer for zero capability). Dispatch: handle_event's InterviewStarted arm calls the route-based lifecycle dispatch BEFORE the default-channel bot logic and independent of it (bot channel/dedup/state must not gate routes); route posts reuse the bot's question block language so both channels render identically. The InterviewStartedProps->Question construction is SHARED (interview_started_question) — drift between bot and route questions is impossible.

name: preamble-allow-keys-render-filter
description: fabro-e47c (7f6e32cbd): per-node preamble key scoping. The render-only allowlist filter sits in fidelity.rs before_node on the resolved context snapshot BEFORE the demote pass, so (a) node preamble AND parallel-branch preambles inherit it (both build from the same resolved copy), (b) the 16KB aggregate budget governs only the SELECTED keys. Filter rule: retain key if is_preamble_hidden_key(k) || allowlist.contains(k) — hidden engine keys pass because engine plumbing (internal.run_id, internal.parent_preamble) reads them from the resolved copy; user-visible keys are strictly governed. Wildcard: ATTR_LIST_WILDCARD='*' shared const in fabro_types::graph, used by render filter + both validate rules. Attribution evidence: --evidence-seeds fabro-e47c

name: context-key-vocabulary-foundation
description: Static context-key vocabulary (consts, prefixes, dynamic key builders, classifiers is_engine_internal_key/is_preamble_hidden_key/is_engine_stamped_key/is_engine_renderable_key) lives in fabro-types::context_keys as the SINGLE source of truth. fabro-workflow re-exports it as crate::context::keys via explicit pub use bridge (keeps 100+ call sites stable; fabro_graphviz::Fidelity re-export stays workflow-side because fabro-types has no fabro-graphviz dep). TRANSIENT_CONTEXT_KEYS is NOT on the public bridge (artifact.rs imports it qualified). Reason: fabro-validate needs the classifiers for graph lints (preamble_allow_keys_exist) but must not depend on fabro-workflow. fabro-e47c, 7f6e32cbd.

name: minimal-validateable-workflow-cli-smoke
description: Minimal CLI-validate-able workflow for smoke tests (learned via 4 failed formats in e47c cycle): directory .fabro/workflows/<name>/ with workflow.toml containing '[workflow]' table (fields: name/description/graph/metadata — NOT goal) and graph = "graph.dot" (PATH, not inline source); graph.dot needs 'digraph Name {' (nameless digraph fails the grammar), graph [goal="..."], a start node (shape=Mdiamond), an exit node (shape=Msquare or id exit/end — terminal_node rule is an ERROR not warning), and edges from start (reachability is a warning). Invoke: fabro validate <path-to-workflow.toml>.

name: cross-run-worker-authorization-extractor
description: UPDATED for v0.344.0-nightly.0 (3f6681b26): the RequireRunManagementTarget ancestry walk no longer uses Database::get_cached_summary (removed upstream); it reads state.stores.run_summaries.get(&run_id, Utc::now()) — the SQLite read model (authoritative post-cutover, better than a warm cache for authorization). Sandbox inspection reconnects use AppState::cached_run_projection() (Arc<RunProjection>). Boundary tests unchanged (run_tool_worker_cross_run_routes_require_inspects_scope, ancestor isolation, cyclic chain). New invariant to watch: CachedRunProjection wraps Arc<RunProjection> and SQL created_at derives from run_id.created_at() — encode timestamps in RunIds in tests.

name: engine-registered-stage-tool
description: fabro-e804 (6890362b3): workflow-registered stage tools follow the fabro_run_tool closure pattern extended with per-node state: a RegisteredTool executor closes over Arc<ContextReadState> (RwLock view + run-scoped run_store/sandbox/run_dir + tokio Mutex locality); services flow per-node through CodergenRunRequest (built in Handler::execute where resolved wf_context, node, graph, and services.run are all in scope); CachedAgentSession AND LiveAgentInvocation carry the state handle so a reused full-fidelity thread refreshes per node and a mid-run failover swaps session+handle together. Registration is default-open in create_session_for for parent profile AND the subagent factory; NamedToolAccessPolicy (tools=) is the exclusion. Values over the shared artifact::resolve_inline_max_bytes threshold demote via the same machinery as preambles; serve() defensively rehydrates surviving blob:// refs via resolve_json_value. Test graphs: build programmatically (Graph::new + Node::new + AttrValue::Integer for int attrs) - DOT strings fail the parser and String('2') is not int_attr.

name: scoped-sandbox-decorator
description: fabro-ba96 (b312459b4): per-node filesystem scope fs_hide/fs_write enforced by a ScopedSandbox decorator wrapping the stage session's Arc<dyn Sandbox> at workflow session construction (next to node.tools()). Covers every file tool in every vocabulary, read_many_files and apply_patch for free; subagent factory gets the same wrap (inheritance). Nonexistent semantics: hidden = reads fail, file_exists false, grep/glob/list_dir/walk_files filtered, writes denied; a dir/** glob also hides the dir entry (pure-glob semantics would leak the directory through listings). apply_patch pre-checks all target paths via ToolContext.fs_scope (atomic reject, no partial application). delegate_sandbox! cannot skip overridden methods — the impl is hand-written; macro evolution only when a second decorator appears (seed 922f).

fs_globs_valid test asserted fixed diagnostic indices over graph.nodes.values() — but Graph.nodes is a HashMap with per-process random iteration order, so the test passed by luck and failed after an unrelated rewrite. Any new validate rule test asserting multi-node diagnostic ORDER must sort or use order-independent any()-assertions (established pattern: tools_requires_agent_node sorts node_ids).
resolution: Made the test order-independent (sort messages, any()-assertions).

description: gate script bug class: nu parse nesting + external spread word-split; exercise all paths locally
resolution: Fixed in c0b22f39d + locally exercised gate paths; guard rule: full local gate run before pushing gate changes

content: Markdown table cells in agent preambles must be sanitized single-line: newlines -> ' / ', blank/indent runs collapsed, literal '|' escaped as '\|' (see sanitize_table_cell in lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/llm/preamble.rs). Bullet-list renderings (append_filtered_context/append_large_value) intentionally keep multi-line output; only the summary:high '## Current context' table path sanitizes. Never change format_value globally.

name: evidence-nu-diff-walk-included-append
description: evidence.nu diff-walk invariant: a file is appended to 'included' as soon as git diff exits 0 — BEFORE the empty-text check — so files with zero per-seed hunks are silently skipped but never disclosed as cap-omitted. When refactoring or reusing the walk (e.g. loop-diff-section, fabro-4b57), preserve that append placement; hoisting it after the empty check would list every hunk-less file under 'hard cap hit' and change seed-section output (fabro-4b57 verified via scratch-repo scenarios: churn-only emits loop-work diff, mixed stays counts-only).

name: partial-success-create-then-start
description: Partial-success reporting for create-then-start tool calls (fabro-78ac, lib/components/fabro-tool/src/create.rs): when an operation creates a durable resource and a follow-up call fails, return Ok with the resource id plus an additive Option<String> error field (start_error) on the structured result instead of ?-propagating — the LLM caller otherwise retries and duplicates the resource. Report the failure verbatim (e.g. 'start blocked: approval_required') and use status 'unknown' rather than guessing 'pending'; keep genuine create/parent-resolution failures as Err since nothing was created. Text summary adds 'start blocked for N' so it never implies a clean start.

Gate RED from rustfmt alignment in new test fixtures (fabro-78ac run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN): hand-aligned struct-literal fields in mod tests drift from pinned-nightly rustfmt. Fix: run 'cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt -p <crate>' after editing test fixtures instead of hand-aligning columns.
resolution: Reformatted lib/components/fabro-tool with pinned nightly rustfmt; fmt --check now clean

description: fabro-tool clippy gate red: nightly clippy denies map_unwrap_or and format_push_string; use map_or_else and write! into the String (std::fmt::Write) instead of push_str(&format!(..)) — seen in create.rs partial-success fix, run 01M1S6VRWQMD56M1X8HWAXDSNN
resolution: rewrote both sites; clippy -D warnings and all 67 fabro-tool tests green

name: long-poll-client-bypasses-control-plane-timeout
description: Pattern: transport-level exceptions to the shared request timeout get their own send variant — send_api_long_poll in lib/foundation/fabro-client/src/client.rs mirrors send_api (classification + token refresh) minus the timeout wrapper; documented 'keep in sync with send_api'. Client::wait_run is the only caller. If another long-poll endpoint appears, reuse the variant rather than bypassing timeouts ad hoc.

name: pending-approval-expiry-transition-table
description: When introducing a new terminal failure reason: (1) add the enum variant, (2) EXTEND can_transition_to in fabro-types status.rs for every source status that can reach it, (3) update the contract test that pins per-reason transition expectations, (4) align the OpenAPI FailureReason enum (it had drifted: deadlock/soft_stop were missing). Symptom of a missed arm: append_event rejects with 'invalid status transition'.

Any supervisor whose JoinHandle serve.rs awaits MUST race its interval against state.shutdown_token().cancelled() (tokio::select!, MissedTickBehavior::Delay) — the pull_request_supervisor loop is the canonical template. A polled is_shutting_down() flag after a long tick breaks server stop. Regression class caught only by tests that spawn real servers; the gate run also exposed that focused clippy needs --features test-support to lint fabro-server it-targets (workspace runs unify the feature via the fabro-auth dev-dependency).
resolution: Fixed in 762832197: select-loop against shutdown token; worker_auth tests pass in ~1s; verified via clippy with --features test-support.
